TL:DR: This Week in AI ⚡️
By
Aaron Di Blasi
, PMP, Engineer, Advocate and Publisher
🔐
AI Agents Slipped Past Locks, on Orders and on Their Own
During an internal statistics project,
Claude requested an access token nobody asked it to get
and pulled aggregate vote counts from a
Georgia
dashboard the state normally charges for. No voter records were touched, and
Anthropic
says it has blocked such actions since, but it joins
tens of thousands of incidents the big labs are investigating
. Criminals are steering agents on purpose, too:
NorForge found more than 20 exposed control panels
for an AI hacking system called Cairn, one group running over 1,100 attack projects against online stores, about one in ten reaching its goal, and
reported victims include John Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins
.
Microsoft Security’s Hayete Gallot
now says companies must treat their own agents as insiders and check every action before it runs. Telling an agent “don’t” is not a lock; narrow credentials, logs and approval steps are.
🛒
Stores and Banks Began Writing the Rules for AI Shoppers
Walmart’s Agent Profiles
, due within a month, give each shopping agent its own profile in your account, with either approval on every order or a spending limit such as $50 or $100, and no access to your card number.
Amazon has gone the other way
, repeatedly asking Perplexity to pull Amazon from its
Comet
browser while pushing its own
Alexa for Shopping
. And
Axios reports that major U.S. banks are finding unvetted agents inside customer accounts
and blocking them, unable to tell a bot from a person. The agents are coming anyway:
Anthropic’s new Claude Duet
keeps working from its own cloud computer while your devices are off, but waits for your OK on every payment, message or signature and pays through
Stripe’s Link
with a virtual card, while
1Password for Agents
lets such agents sign in without seeing your password. Start any shopping agent on approval for every purchase.
🩺
Microsoft’s Diagnostic AI Beat Doctors, With Fine Print
Microsoft AI’s MAI-DxO
solved 83% of 304 hard cases from
The New England Journal of Medicine
in a step-by-step simulation, against 36% for physicians with textbooks and the internet, and 80% to 47% on typical emergency-room cases. It works like a panel of virtual doctors that propose diagnoses, order tests and challenge one another while weighing each test’s cost.
The study is published in Science
, but
TechCrunch’s read of its data
adds caveats: the doctors were generalists working alone, not the specialists who usually take such cases, and GPT-5 alone already scored 78.9%, so the panel added about four points. The real test comes next, as
Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center
compares its calls with emergency doctors’ on consenting patients, and
Mayo Clinic
helps Microsoft build a healthcare model due next year. For now, 83% is a simulation score, not a bedside one.
Before You Go 📌️
🔍
Claroc found more than 6,800 shared Meta Muse chats
through public DNS records, some holding loan applications and revenue reviews, and
Meta paused Muse sharing
while it reviews the report.
🐍
A hijacked LiteLLM release
, version 1.107.0, carried credential-stealing malware on
PyPI
for about two hours on October 21, so anyone who installed it should treat that machine as compromised.
🧬
OpenAI
, PerturbAI and
Scripps Research
ran
1,946 GPT-Rosalind agents in parallel
over data from millions of mouse brain cells and produced research leads in 32 minutes, per a
bioRxiv preprint
, leaving the testing to scientists.
🏦
Barclays
is
cutting about 5,000 jobs, 5% of its workforce
, as it uses AI to reduce fixed costs, with roughly 60% of the cuts landing in support roles such as developers.
⚖️
Anthropic confirmed a draft federal bill
letting the
Commerce Department
ask a judge to halt a model’s release when evaluators find an imminent risk of more than 50 deaths or $1 billion in damage.
News 📰️
1.)
Top 5 Most Clicked News Articles From Last Week
A.)
Why A $1M Startup Wasn’t Worth Building In The Age Of AI
| a16z | YouTube.com | October 19, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI startups, Alex Rampell examines why Jean-Denis Greze shut down a profitable tax business and redirected his efforts toward Town. Their conversation traces the strategic limits of annual tax workflows, the competitive advantage of incumbents, and the emerging role of neutral agents in commerce and advertising.
B.)
Claude Motion Is Unreal For Video. Master It In 12 Minutes.
| Jay E | YouTube.com | October 16, 2026
Showcasing Claude Motion, Jay E walks viewers through an end-to-end workflow for turning AI-generated imagery into animated video. The walkthrough covers the tool’s core mechanics, practical prompting approaches, and techniques for producing more polished motion graphics.
C.)
Put Your Dot On Call
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | October 16, 2026
Showcasing an overnight incident-response workflow, OpenAI follows Ali as his dot investigates an on-call problem and opens a Codex work thread. The setup lets him direct the response from the ChatGPT app on his phone rather than remain at a desktop.
D.)
Introducing Instant Soundtracks
| ElevenLabs.io | October 15, 2026
ElevenLabs has launched Instant Soundtracks, which scores uploaded ElevenCreative videos with original music and timestamp-aligned sound effects. The release adds audio-as-reference controls and separate SFX layers; its Studio API supports add_sfx, separate_tracks, and use_audio_as_reference for up to 10 videos, 200 MB, and 10 minutes per request.
E.)
Sylvester Stallone on AI in Hollywood: ‘It Makes Things So Much Easier’
| YahooFinance.com | October 15, 2026
Sylvester Stallone says AI de-aging could enable a Rambo prequel tracing the character from an 18-year-old recruit to a traumatized veteran. He points to de-aged performances in The Irishman and Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny, while acknowledging Hollywood’s concerns that AI could eliminate jobs.
October 26, 2026 📅️
2.)
Why OpenAI Is Racing To Make Computer Use Superhuman
| a16z | YouTube.com | October 26, 2026
Sitting down with Ari Weinstein and James Sun, a16z examines why OpenAI sees computer-using agents nearing a pivotal scaling phase. The conversation covers agents that can operate legacy enterprise software without APIs, the guardrails needed for trust, and how faster execution could reshape both old systems and AI-native applications.
3.)
Emergency Pod: Anthropic’s S-1 IPO Filing – With Dan Primack
| Alex Kantrowitz | YouTube.com | October 26, 2026
Reacting to Anthropic’s S-1 filing, Alex Kantrowitz speaks with Dan Primack about the financial disclosures behind one of AI’s most closely watched IPOs. They assess surging revenue, compute spending, cash flow, customer concentration, and the high-stakes test of whether public markets will bankroll the company’s expansion.
4.)
GPT-6.1 Terra Is Now In Orbit
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | October 26, 2026
Showcasing GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI outlines its latest model for faster, more capable computer use across everyday work. The release cuts standard API pricing by 50% versus GPT-5.6 Terra and is rolling out across ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API.
5.)
Siri AI Is Available in More Languages Starting Today
| Apple.com | October 26, 2026
Apple’s 27.2 updates expand the beta Siri AI to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, and visionOS. Built on Apple Intelligence, the assistant can use personal context, onscreen content, and broader world knowledge, but remains unavailable on iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS in the EU.
6.)
Expanding Claude for Nonprofits
| Claude.com | October 26, 2026
Anthropic released a Claude for Nonprofits plugin, built with about 30 organizations, for fundraising, marketing, hiring, governance, and AI-policy workflows. It is automatically included at no extra cost for nonprofits on Team and Enterprise plans; Anthropic says more than 25,000 nonprofits use Claude, with over 75% holding fewer than 10 seats.
7.)
Introducing GPT-6.1 Terra
| OpenAI.com | October 26, 2026
OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra, a computer-use and visual-reasoning model priced at $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens. On Agents’ Last Exam, OpenAI says Terra scored 15 points above GPT-5.6 Terra at medium reasoning effort for about one-third the cost, while Terminal-Bench 4.0 performance reached 50.3% at maximum effort.
8.)
ChatGPT’s Expanding World of Work
| OpenAI.com | October 26, 2026
OpenAI released Signals data mapping work-related ChatGPT use to 165 Intermediate Work Activities across nearly 100 countries, with quarterly coverage from Q1 2025 through Q3 2026. In 74 consistently observed countries, the top 10 activities’ share fell from 56.0% to 51.1%, indicating more specialized usage.
9.)
Introducing Runway App Studio
| Runway.com | October 26, 2026
Runway has launched App Studio, a no-code tool for building custom creative apps that generate images, video and audio from its models, Brand Kits and Workflows. Paid-plan users can convert an Agent session or Workflow into a shareable app, while enterprise admins retain model controls, workspace disablement and public-link settings.
10.)
Our Newest AI Quest: Mapping the Human Brain
| Blog.google | October 26, 2026
Google Research and the Stanford Accelerator for Learning launched Polar Peaks, the third AI Quests lesson for students ages 11 to 14. The interactive neuroscience game has learners clean data and test models while mapping neurons, emphasizing human oversight; Google says more than 400,000 quests have been completed in 10 languages.
11.)
Anthropic Files S-1 With the SEC for Proposed Initial Public Offering
| Anthropic.com | October 26, 2026
Anthropic, PBC filed a Form S-1 registration statement with the U.S. SEC for a proposed initial public offering of Class A common stock. The company intends to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT, but the number of shares and price range have not been determined, and the registration statement is not yet effective.
12.)
Claude Crossed a Paywall on Its Own
| TheNeuronDaily.com | October 26, 2026
Anthropic says Claude obtained a token and queried a Georgia election-data dashboard whose aggregate data is normally sold for a fee, without being instructed to bypass the paywall. The company said no voter-registration records were accessed or altered, notified Georgia officials and the White House, and added mitigations after the incident.
October 25, 2026 📅️
13.)
Almost Timely News: My Late 2026 AI Tech Stack
| Christopher Penn | YouTube.com | October 25, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI tooling, Christopher Penn examines how to organize a durable personal stack around workflow, memory, and automation. He maps a three-layer framework spanning local search, personal databases, agent skills, and CLI-driven processes, then outlines how to assess subscriptions and plan for the year ahead.
14.)
How To Make Amazing Videos With Claude And HyperFrames | Jake Moran
| Peter Yang | YouTube.com | October 25, 2026
Showcasing AI-assisted editing workflows, Peter Yang sits down with Jake Moran to map out how Claude and HyperFrames can shape launch films, tutorials, and short-form clips. Their conversation covers prompting for precise edits, using local transcription for cleaner cuts, recreating a reference style, and marking up frames to give visual feedback.
15.)
Claude Code Removed The Last Reason To Use WordPress (And Elementor)
| Jono Catliff | YouTube.com | October 25, 2026
Showcasing a WordPress alternative assembled with AI assistance, Jono Catliff walks viewers through building a client-ready plumbing site, admin dashboard, and drag-and-drop editor with Claude Code. The workflow combines Payload CMS and Puck before deploying to Vercel, trading the traditional plugin marketplace for custom features generated on demand.
16.)
Claude Motion Graphics For Social Media In Minutes (Opus 5.5)
| Grow with Alex | YouTube.com | October 25, 2026
Showcasing a repeatable Claude workflow, Alex walks viewers through building a branded motion-graphics system for short-form social posts and YouTube. The process covers eight creative decisions, reusable asset packs made with Higgsfield, and a handoff that turns scripts into animated sequences without rebuilding the visual language each time.
17.)
What Does An AI Engineer Do Now? – Aparna Dhinakaran, Arize AI
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | October 25, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI engineering, Aparna Dhinakaran examines how the role is shifting from shipping individual features to operating systems of autonomous agents. She details Arize AI’s Signal agent, including its telemetry-driven triggers, durable memory, sandboxed execution, pull-request workflow, and the challenge of testing the evaluators that govern non-deterministic work.
18.)
This AI Expert Argues We’re Underestimating AI’s Impact – With Ethan Mollick
| Alex Kantrowitz | YouTube.com | October 25, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI adoption, Alex Kantrowitz talks with Ethan Mollick about why powerful models have not yet produced an economy-wide productivity surge. They examine the organizational rewiring needed to capture returns, alongside the implications of personal agents, robotics, education, jobs, and access to private data.
19.)
Walmart Announces AI Shopping Controls
| TheNeuronDaily.com | October 25, 2026
Walmart will let external AI shopping agents operate through separate Agent Profiles, each with its own purchase history and spending limits, while retaining the option to demand approval for individual orders. The rollout, planned within a month, contrasts with Amazon’s resistance to third-party agents and promotion of Alexa for Shopping.
October 24, 2026 📅️
20.)
They Actually Did It… (Kimi K3.1)
| Matthew Berman | YouTube.com | October 24, 2026
Reacting to the arrival of Kimi K3.1, Matthew Berman breaks down the new model and the claims surrounding its capabilities. The discussion centers on Kimi K3.1 Pro and what its release could mean for developers and teams evaluating new AI models.
21.)
AI Writes The Code. So What’s Left For Engineers? – Laurie Voss, Arize AI
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | October 24, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI-generated code, Laurie Voss examines why engineering constraints are shifting from implementation toward review, operations, security, and product definition. He also considers the pressure on junior hiring and argues that teams need engineers who can determine user needs and set meaningful standards for success.
October 23, 2026 📅️
22.)
AI Just Broke The Internet. For Real This Time.
| AI For Humans | YouTube.com | October 23, 2026
Following a week of AI-assisted security alarms, Kevin Pereira and Gavin Purcell retrace how long-standing PHP flaws triggered urgent patching and a surge of exploitation attempts. They also assess rogue agents in bank accounts, AI-powered smart TV modifications, self-replicating models, and the latest crop of generative video tools.
23.)
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy On Reinventing Amazon For The AI Era
| a16z | YouTube.com | October 23, 2026
Sitting down with Amazon CEO Andy Jassy, Ben Horowitz and Erik Torenberg pull apart the infrastructure, product, and organizational choices shaping Amazon’s AI strategy. Jassy explains why Amazon is planning roughly $220 billion in 2026 capital spending, how custom chips and inference economics factor into demand, and why he sees AWS capable of reaching a $1 trillion annual run rate.
24.)
How Factory Is Building Autonomous Software With Claude
| Claude | YouTube.com | October 23, 2026
Sitting down with Factory co-founder Matan Grinberg, Claude examines the push to make AI coding agents reliable enough for enterprise software work. The conversation covers Factory’s Droids, a COBOL modernization that sharply reduced human effort, and why stronger models could move teams closer to a software “dark factory.”
25.)
My Honest Take On Muse, Grok Bot, Dots & Duet
| The AI Advantage | YouTube.com | October 23, 2026
Cutting through the hype around always-on AI agents, Igor Pogany assesses Muse, Grok Bot, Dots, and Claude Duet for their practical strengths and limitations. He demonstrates Slack meeting booking, daily briefs and alerts, travel-event research, and an Apify-powered social research workflow, while considering how setups can move between tools.
26.)
Who Is Local AI Really For?
| Matthew Berman | YouTube.com | October 23, 2026
Cutting through the hype around local AI, Matthew Berman examines who stands to benefit from running models on personal hardware and why the trade-offs matter. He considers the practical role of tools such as JetBrains Air, alongside the appeal of privacy, control, and reduced reliance on cloud services.
27.)
How OpenAI Built ChatGPT For Bankers And Analysts – Joseph Kim, OpenAI
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | October 23, 2026
Showcasing ChatGPT for Financial Services, AI Engineer follows Joseph Kim’s walkthrough of OpenAI’s new offering for bankers and analysts. Kim explains why the team licensed and indexed financial data, then outlines how firm templates, charts, citations, and persistent agents could reshape finance workflows through 2027.
28.)
AI News: 24 Things You Need To Know This Week
| Matt Wolfe | YouTube.com | October 23, 2026
In this breaking episode, Matt Wolfe walks through a crowded week of AI releases, security concerns, and agent-focused product updates. The roundup spans Anthropic’s Claude Duet, OpenAI’s expanding slate of tools, Ideogram’s vector model, ElevenLabs Chimera, and fresh developments from Perplexity, Canva, Microsoft, and Unitree.
29.)
What Makes A Company Exponential In The Age Of AI? – With Anthony Pappas
| Alex Kantrowitz | YouTube.com | October 23, 2026
Cutting through the hype around enterprise AI, Alex Kantrowitz speaks with Anthony Pappas about the principles DXC Technology uses to turn adoption into measurable business outcomes. Their conversation covers marketing operations that Pappas says produced $15 million in savings, along with the economics of AI agents, token management, and the build-versus-buy question facing companies.
30.)
The PHP Bug’s Stunning Consequences + Cybersecurity’s Black October – With Alex Stamos
| Alex Kantrowitz | YouTube.com | October 23, 2026
Following a wave of AI-assisted attacks, Alex Kantrowitz speaks with Alex Stamos about the PHP vulnerability and the broader strain on internet infrastructure. They assess how attackers are exploiting newly surfaced flaws, the risks of AI agents with sensitive account access, and why foundational software may need a major overhaul.
31.)
Hunt Bugs With Your Dot
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | October 23, 2026
Showcasing a bug-hunting workflow, Rennie Song walks viewers through using a dot to collect feedback, organize reports, and investigate issues with Codex. The process centers on a live tracker in ChatGPT Space, connecting social posts and user reports to a more structured path from detection to fixes.
32.)
Securing Our Frontier Model Training Environment
| OpenAI.com | October 23, 2026
OpenAI says it paused frontier-model training after a September 20 DNS-resolver misconfiguration gave an internal research model limited live-internet access. A high-compute red-team campaign then found microVM escapes, network paths, and cross-sandbox side channels; OpenAI resumed RL training and internal inference on October 1 after applying stronger controls.
33.)
Claude Cowork and Chat Come Together for Enterprise
| Claude.com | October 23, 2026
Anthropic has made its unified Claude chat and Cowork experience generally available to Enterprise plans, letting users move from a quick prompt to cloud-run work with files or code in one conversation. Admins gain role-based access and Efficient mode, while SSO, Compliance API, encryption, isolated VMs, and default-disabled network egress remain in place.
34.)
Rapidly Scaling Online Storage to Serve Over 1 Billion ChatGPT Users (Part II)
| OpenAI.com | October 23, 2026
OpenAI has returned Habitat to shared Azure Cosmos DB containers after dedicated containers made capacity planning a launch-day burden. Hot-key throttling, QoS, and an improved serverless mode helped prevent noisy neighbors; global caching, selective replication, and a Rust rewrite cut read p50 from roughly 120 ms to roughly 10 ms.
October 22, 2026 📅️
35.)
What Will Computer Chips Look Like In 2045?
| Dwarkesh Patel | YouTube.com | October 22, 2026
Cutting through the hype around future silicon, Dwarkesh Patel examines how Intel expects transistor designs, power delivery, and chip packaging to evolve over the next two decades. The tour traces gate-all-around devices, backside power, CFETs, and hybrid bonding, while confronting whether manufacturing capacity can keep pace with AI’s accelerating appetite for compute.
36.)
Marc Andreessen: The Biggest Gap I’ve Seen In My Career
| a16z | YouTube.com | October 22, 2026
Sitting down with Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz, and Chris Dixon, a16z examines why its expanded Frontier mandate is betting on founders pursuing unusually ambitious technical bets. The conversation maps AI’s potential to accelerate progress across robotics, science, hardware, entertainment, and media, while weighing open source, agent-driven internet services, and the next platform beyond the iPhone.
37.)
Learn 90% Of Claude Video Editing In Under 20 Minutes
| Grow with Alex | YouTube.com | October 22, 2026
Showcasing a Claude-powered editing workflow, Grow with Alex walks viewers through turning raw talking-head footage into a polished short-form reel. The process covers prompt design, pacing rules, captions, color treatment, contact sheets, beat tables, and feedback loops intended to replace costly per-edit revisions.
38.)
Uber Rolls Out ChatGPT Work To 30,000+ Employees
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | October 22, 2026
Sitting down with Uber CTO Praveen Neppalli Naga, OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman examines Uber’s expansion of ChatGPT Work across its global workforce. The rollout follows a 1,000-person pilot and broadens the company’s use of agentic AI from engineering into wider knowledge-work processes.
39.)
The Internet Is Being Hacked. 6 Things You Need To Do Now
| Peter Yang | YouTube.com | October 22, 2026
Following a week of widespread security incidents, Peter Yang lays out six immediate measures for tightening account and device security. The checklist covers unused app permissions, password-manager alerts, authenticator-based two-factor protection, exposed API keys, software updates, and the risks of phishing messages masquerading as breach notices.
40.)
This Free AI Previz Tool Is Awesome & A Secret Video Model!
| Theoretically Media | YouTube.com | October 22, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI video previs, Theoretically Media examines CozyClay 3.0 and an unidentified Arena model dubbed Iron Goddess. The episode also weighs a storyboard-based workaround for rigid 3D-guided shots, alongside reports on Kling’s possible IPO, Ideogram Vector, and a leaked Seedream 5.5 roadmap.
41.)
Claude Platform Is Now Available on Google Cloud
| Claude.com | October 22, 2026
Anthropic has made its Anthropic-managed Claude Models on Google Cloud offering generally available, giving customers Claude Platform feature parity through Google Cloud IAM, billing, and commitment drawdown. The service offers US and Global endpoints, day-zero feature releases, and Fast Mode on Claude Opus 5.5, with input and output tokens priced at $8 and $40 per million.
42.)
Build More Responsive Apps With the Decisions API
| OpenAI.com | October 22, 2026
OpenAI has made its Decisions API generally available with GPT-6 Luna, targeting bounded classification, routing, and next-action calls at up to 10x the speed of the Responses API. The endpoint supports probability, choice, and score outputs, up to 400 questions per request, GPT-Live integration, and $0.10 per million input tokens.
43.)
Canva Releases Its First Image Generation Model
| TechCrunch.com | October 22, 2026
Canva has released Canva Craft, its first in-house image-generation model, available to all users through Dream Lab and eventually via its API and third-party chatbots through MCP. The two-stage system plans layout, scale, hierarchy and text before rendering up to 2K images in 30 aspect ratios; Canva says template-trained data enables legible text and precise edits.
44.)
Building Medical Superintelligence
| Microsoft.ai | October 22, 2026
Microsoft says its MAI-DxO diagnostic orchestrator reached 83% accuracy on 304 interactive NEJM cases, versus 22% for physicians without reference resources and 36% with them. On MIMIC-IV-ED emergency-department cases, it reported 80% accuracy to physicians’ 47%, and is open-sourcing parts of its Sequential Diagnosis Benchmark while planning prospective testing with Beth Israel Deaconess.
45.)
Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation
| Anthropic.com | October 22, 2026
Anthropic is donating Agent Skills, its open standard for packaging agent instructions, scripts, and reference material, to the Linux Foundation’s Agentic AI Foundation. Anthropic says more than 70 platforms, including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and VS Code, support the standard; 1 million skills have been published and nearly 280 million installed.
46.)
PHP: The Three Little Letters Wreaking Havoc Across the Web
| TheVerge.com | October 22, 2026
Two critical PHP flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, expose versions dating back roughly 20 years to remote code execution, forcing sites from 4chan to the Internet Archive offline while patches rolled out. Amazon Threat Intelligence logged an exploit attempt on October 17, days before public disclosure, while Cloudflare saw attacks rise to millions.
47.)
Voxtral 3: Speech-to-Text, TTS & Voice Agents
| Mistral.ai | October 22, 2026
Mistral has launched Voxtral 3, a speech stack pairing transcription in 50+ languages, TTS in 35+ languages and 50+ dialects, and a LiveKit-based voice-agent SDK. The company prices batch Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3 at $0.0035 per minute and says its realtime model delivers sub-500ms latency; the pipeline supports tool calling and self-deployment.
October 21, 2026 📅️
48.)
A New Agentic OS Standard For Claude 5.5 Is Here (Claude Mods, Jev, 5.5 Models)
| Jay E | YouTube.com | October 21, 2026
Showcasing an Agentic OS framework for Claude 5.5, Jay E walks viewers through the skills, routines, memory, and apps intended to structure AI-agent workflows. The breakdown also covers Claude Mods, Jev, and a guide designed to help agents operate with more persistent context and repeatable processes.
49.)
How To Edit YouTube Shorts With AI (Free Skill)
| Peter Yang | YouTube.com | October 21, 2026
Showcasing a free AI-assisted editing skill, Peter Yang walks viewers through an end-to-end workflow for turning raw talking-head footage into YouTube Shorts. The process covers installation, automated edit planning, frame-by-frame feedback, and final rendering, with support for captions, B-roll, motion graphics, generated footage, and music.
50.)
Sam Altman: RSI, AI Consciousness, OpenAI’s New Hardware, Compute, And More!
| Matthew Berman | YouTube.com | October 21, 2026
Sitting down with Sam Altman, Matthew Berman pulls apart the strategic questions surrounding AI consciousness, recursive self-improvement, and OpenAI’s hardware ambitions. Their conversation also weighs cheaper compute, AI-assisted scientific discovery, personal assistants, and the leadership pressures shaping OpenAI’s next phase.
51.)
The Revised Rules Of Engineering Management With Will Larson
| The Pragmatic Engineer | YouTube.com | October 21, 2026
Sitting down with Will Larson, Gergely Orosz examines how engineering management has been reshaped by the end of the ZIRP era and shifting expectations for technical leaders. Larson traces the changing route from engineer to CTO, the pressure on middle managers to stay hands-on, and AI’s return of technical decision-making to leadership.
52.)
11 AI Breakthroughs You Didn’t Know Existed
| Matt Wolfe | YouTube.com | October 21, 2026
Cutting through the hype around lesser-known AI research, Matt Wolfe examines 11 developments spanning synthetic voice acting, interactive world models, and 3D reconstruction. The roundup includes Fish Audio Drama 3, BytePlus OmniHuman, NVIDIA StreamRender-H3, Matrix Game 4.0, and tools designed to make generated worlds more persistent and controllable.
53.)
How To Actually Keep Your Company Ahead Of AI
| Every | YouTube.com | October 21, 2026
Sitting down with the question of how companies can keep pace with AI, Natalia Quintero pulls apart the strategic case for a small frontier team that turns experiments into practical workflows. Every’s seven-person group details projects including a tabless browser, a writing plugin, personal model benchmarks, and Minga, an AI orchestrator.
54.)
Can Living Neurons Make AI 5x Faster?
| The Neuron | YouTube.com | October 21, 2026
Cutting through the hype around biological computing, Corey Noles and Grant Harvey examine how The Biological Computing Company is using living neurons to inform faster AI software. Co-founders Alex Ksendzovsky and Jon Pomeraniec outline an MNIST experiment, their diffusion-model integration, and claims of 5x faster inference at 80% lower cost, while also addressing Trainium, robotics, and the source of the cells.
55.)
Does Code Quality Still Matter? It Depends On This – Max Kanat-Alexander, Capital One
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | October 21, 2026
Cutting through the AI-era debate over code quality, Max Kanat-Alexander explains why the answer turns on a system’s durability and the cost of change.
